items.title: Delhi court issues non-bailable warrant against Dhruv Rathee in 2018 defamation case
items.summary: A Delhi court on Monday issued a non-bailable warrant against Youtuber Dhruv Rathee in a 2018 defamation case filed by Vikas Sankrityayan, alias Vikas Pandey. The order was passed by Judicial Magistrate First Class Anam Rais Khan passed the order. The matter will be heard next on December 3. The case stemmed from a video made by Rathee in May 2018 alleging that Pandey, who he described as a senior functionary of the BJP IT Cell, had offered a bribe of ₹50 lakh to a person named Mahavir Prasad to defame him. Rathee subsequently alleged on Twitter that the BJP IT Cell had attempted to bribe someone to malign his reputation. The video tweeted on Rathee's handle was retweeted by the then Chief Minister of Delhi Arvind Kejriwal. This prompted Pandey to initiate defamation proceedings against both Kejriwal and Rathee. The Court had earlier issued bailable warrant on Rathee . On October 12 , the Court had allowed an application seeking early hearing and the issuance of dasti (by hand) summons against Rathee. This was after advocate Samaksh Sharma for the complainant argued that summons had remained unserved for several years as Rathee primarily resides abroad. #Breaking Delhi court issues

items.title: Allahabad High Court Bar Association to impose ₹5,000 fine on advocates recording reels inside court premises
items.summary: The Allahabad High Court Bar Association has announced that it will impose a ₹5,000 fine on advocates who take photographs or record videos or reels inside the court premises, including the courtrooms and corridors of the High Court. In a notice circulated by the Bar President CP Upadhyaya on November 18, the Bar Association said, "All respected advocates are hereby informed that making videos/reels and taking photographs inside the premises, courtrooms, and corridors of the Hon'ble High Court is strictly prohibited. If any advocate or any other person is caught committing such an act inside the premises, they will have to immediately deposit a fine of Rs. 5,000/- in the office of the High Court Bar Association, Allahabad." The Bar Association said that disciplinary action will also be initiated against such advocates, and warned them of the termination of their membership. "Therefore, all respected advocates are appealed not to engage in such acts that tarnish the image of this profession," it said in the notice.
